sections.html:
Murray sits at the heart of the Salt Lake Valley and touches Taylorsville, Holladay, South Salt Lake, Millcreek and West Jordan. The Jordan River is its western edge, and Big and Little Cottonwood Creeks both join the river inside city limits. Elevation is about 4,301 feet, and the city spreads over 12.32 square miles.

Residents numbered 50,637 in 2020, up from 46,746 in 2010. Here are the housing figures a seller is most likely to be asked about.

Housing measureMurray
Population density4,109.5 per square mile

sections.h2: From smelter town to hospital campus
sections.html:
Settled in 1848 and named for a territorial governor, Murray incorporated as a third class city on January 3, 1903. Smelting paid the bills early on. The first smelter went up around 1870, ASARCO formed in 1899, and its lead smelter shut down in 1949. The stacks came down in 2000, and Intermountain Healthcare bought the land. Intermountain Medical Center replaced Cottonwood Hospital in 2007 and remains a major employer.

Fashion Place Mall opened in the 1970s, and State Street turned into a corridor of car dealerships. House age and condition vary a lot from one Murray street to the next.

Few Utah cities do what Murray does: its own police, fire, power, water, sewer, library and parks departments. City utility billing covers power, water, sewer, garbage and stormwater in many areas, while other providers handle addresses where the city has no lines. Murray City Power has been publicly owned since 1913 and serves about 18,000 customers, 82 percent residential and 18 percent commercial and industrial.

  • Call utility billing at (801) 264-2626 to ask how a final reading and a service transfer work for your address.
  • The office is at 10 East 4800 South, Suite 160. Pay only through the city's own website, because look-alike sites go after Murray customers.
  • Before you list, find out whether your water and sewer come from the city or another provider.

Three TRAX stations serve Murray: Murray North, Murray Central and Fashion Place West, on the Blue and Red lines. Murray Central is also where TRAX meets FrontRunner, which began running in December 2012, and it is the only such connection outside Salt Lake City. Interstate 15 and Interstate 215 both cross the city, and the average trip to work is 20.7 minutes. Put the distance to a station in your listing.

Murray has its own school district, created January 1, 1906, with ten schools and more than 6,000 students: Murray High School, Hillcrest Junior High, Riverview Junior High and seven elementaries (Grant, Horizon, Liberty, Longview, McMillan, Parkside and Viewmont). Some addresses belong to Granite School District instead, which runs Cottonwood High School and Woodstock Elementary inside Murray. The street decides which one applies.

  • Bergertown, south of 4800 South along Little Cottonwood Creek, started as a Swiss immigrant enclave.
  • The Murray Downtown Historic District runs along State Street.
  • Murray City Park covers 22 acres, with a baseball stadium and an amphitheatre.
  • The Jordan River Parkway trail follows the west edge.

The city counts residential rentals as a business, so an owner needs a current Murray business license. One license covers every rental held by the same legal entity, and hiring a property manager does not replace it. Licenses cannot be transferred between owners or addresses, which means a buyer who keeps your tenants must apply on their own. Operating without a license, or after one lapses, brings a penalty of 100 percent of the past-due fees under City Code 5.04.280. Renewal notices go out on the first of the month the license expires, and a postmark does not prove timely receipt.

Accessory dwelling units are limited to one per lot, and the owner must live in the main house or the unit. A detached unit needs a lot of at least 10,000 square feet, a height of 20 feet or less and a single story, and it cannot sit in the front yard. Renting an ADU for stays under 30 days is prohibited. Before the city accepts an application, an affidavit about occupancy and short-term rental terms must be recorded with the Salt Lake County Recorder, so the document is on record with the county.

If tenants live in the house, line up three documents before you talk to buyers: the lease, your current business license and any recorded ADU affidavit. Because the license does not travel with the property, a buyer who wants to keep renting will need to apply immediately after closing. Say that out loud early, and agree on who tells the tenant and when.

The Wasatch Fault and soft lake sediments shape building risk along the whole Wasatch Front. Many areas rest on Lake Bonneville sediments, which raises liquefaction risk, and the Salt Lake City segment last broke 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. The odds of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake within 50 years are put at 57 percent.

In practice, expect a buyer's inspector to flag chimney bracing, an unstrapped water heater or foundation cracking, and decide ahead of time how you will respond. Because Big and Little Cottonwood Creeks both run through the city, ask the county for flood zone information if your lot is near either one.

sections.h2: Property tax dates and deed recording
sections.html:
Salt Lake County values and bills Murray property, and its calendar sets every date you need.

  • Value is fixed as of January 1.
  • Valuation notices arrive in July and August, and the Board of Equalization window runs 45 days from the original mailing.
  • Tax notices go out by November 1.
  • November 30 is the last day to pay without penalty, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent on December 1.

Before a deed is recorded, the county asks for white 8.5 by 11 inch paper, a legible caption on the first page, the grantee's name and mailing address, and a legal description. The grantor's name must match across the title, the document, the notary acknowledgment and the signature. Call the recorder for the current recording fee before you sign.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Murray
sections.html: A cash sale still closes through a title company, minus a buyer's lender. We look at the house as it is and make an offer, and the title company takes care of signing and files the deed with the county. Murray callers often have an inherited home, rentals with tenants or a house that needs work. Mention any lease, rental license or accessory unit when you call so the offer reflects it. If the number does not fit, you can decline.

faqs.q: What school district is Murray, Utah in?
faqs.a: Most of Murray is in Murray City School District, which has ten schools. Granite School District runs Cottonwood High School and Woodstock Elementary inside the city, so confirm the district for a specific address.
Murray City Power, a municipal utility created in 1913, serves about 18,000 customers. The city also supplies water, sewer and garbage service in many areas, and other providers cover the rest.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent out a Murray house?
faqs.a: Yes. Murray treats residential rentals as a business, and one license covers all rentals owned by the same legal entity. It cannot be transferred to a buyer.

faqs.q: Can I rent an accessory dwelling unit short term in Murray?
faqs.a: No. The city prohibits renting an ADU for stays shorter than 30 days, and the owner must live on the property.

faqs.q: When are Murray property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay current-year real property tax without penalty. Taxes become delinquent on December 1.
